questions.q: When does this lesson say fine-tuning is worth doing, instead of just prompting a general-purpose model?
options: When a general model consistently underperforms on a specific domain or format, and enough labeled examples exist to teach it the difference
Every single time any Cortex function is used, with no exceptions
Only when the model needs to be translated into another programming language
Never — fine-tuning is described as always worse than prompting
questions.explain: Fine-tuning targets the narrower case of consistent underperformance on a specific domain, where enough labeled data exists to adapt the model rather than engineer an ever-longer prompt.

questions.q: What SQL function launches a Cortex fine-tuning job?
options: SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.FINETUNE
SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.TRAIN_MODEL
AI_FINETUNE
SNOWFLAKE.ML.CREATE_MODEL
questions.explain: SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.FINETUNE accepts 'CREATE', 'SHOW', 'DESCRIBE', and 'CANCEL' to manage fine-tuning jobs.

questions.q: What technique does Cortex Fine-Tuning use under the hood, and why does it matter?
options: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) — it freezes the base model's weights and trains only small adapter matrices, making fine-tuning economical
Full retraining of every parameter in the base model from scratch
A manual, human-only editing process with no machine learning involved
Simple keyword replacement in the model's output text
questions.explain: LoRA is parameter-efficient: the base model stays frozen and only small added matrices are trained, which is why fine-tuning can be offered as a managed SQL function.

questions.q: Where must training and validation data come from for Cortex Fine-Tuning?
options: Tables or views already inside the customer's own Snowflake account, referenced by SQL queries
An uploaded file sent to a third-party training service outside Snowflake
Public datasets hosted by Snowflake with no customer data involved
A separate cloud storage bucket unrelated to Snowflake
questions.explain: The FINETUNE function points at SQL queries against your own Snowflake tables — training data never leaves Snowflake's security perimeter.

questions.q: What is the key capability gap between Cortex Training (public preview) and basic Cortex Fine-Tuning (GA), per this lesson?
options: Cortex Training supports reinforcement learning on proprietary data, which basic LoRA-based Fine-Tuning does not offer
Cortex Training is free while Cortex Fine-Tuning always costs money
Cortex Fine-Tuning requires data to leave Snowflake, while Cortex Training does not
There is no difference between the two services
questions.explain: Cortex Training, built on the ArcticTraining framework with managed GPU pools, adds reinforcement learning on proprietary data and support for more model families beyond what LoRA-based Cortex Fine-Tuning offers.
